Replace the field validator with @model_validator(mode='after') that reads and sets fields on self.

Replace the field validator with @model_validator(mode='after') that reads and sets fields on self.
Replace @root_validator with @model_validator; pre=True becomes mode='before' on a classmethod taking the raw dict, otherwise mode='after' on an instance method returning self.
Replace @root_validator with @model_validator(mode='before') on a classmethod that works on the input dict.

Remove Config.json_encoders; add @field_serializer for the affected fields (or a PlainSerializer in Annotated) that produces the same output, and move other Config keys to model_config = ConfigDict(...).
Remove json_encoders and add a @model_serializer(mode='wrap') that formats datetimes the same way.
Turn the __root__ model into a pydantic.RootModel[...] subclass and use .root instead of .__root__; parse with model_validate.
Replace the __root__ model with a TypeAdapter over the inner type plus a plain helper class.
Replace Model.update_forward_refs() with Model.model_rebuild().

Replace @validator with @field_validator plus @classmethod; pre=True becomes mode='before', each_item=True becomes validating the list items in the function, always=True becomes validate_default=True on the Field.
Move the check into an Annotated type with AfterValidator / BeforeValidator.
Replace @validate_arguments with @validate_call.
Rename removed config keys to their v2 names in model_config = ConfigDict(...) (allow_mutation=False->frozen=True, orm_mode->from_attributes, fields={...alias}->Field(alias=...)).
Replace @validator with @field_validator plus @classmethod, take info: ValidationInfo and read earlier fields from info.data instead of values.
Replace the field validator with @model_validator(mode='after') that reads and sets fields on self.

Replace `__get_validators__` with `__get_pydantic_core_schema__(cls, source_type, handler)` that returns `core_schema.no_info_plain_validator_function(cls.validate)`, importing `core_schema` from `pydantic_core`. This preserves the existing normalization and validation behavior while using Pydantic v2's schema API.

Replace the `PostCode` subclass and its `__get_validators__` hook with a `PostCode = Annotated[str, BeforeValidator(validate_post_code)]` alias. Move the current normalization and length/digit checks into `validate_post_code`, return the normalized string, and import `Annotated` and `BeforeValidator`.
Rename removed config keys to their v2 names in model_config = ConfigDict(...) (allow_mutation=False->frozen=True, orm_mode->from_attributes, fields={...alias}->Field(alias=...)).
Replace Model.parse_obj(data) with Model.model_validate(data).
Replace Model.parse_obj(data) with Model(**data).
Replace Model.parse_raw(body) with Model.model_validate_json(body).
Replace Model.parse_raw(body) with Model.model_validate(json.loads(body)).
Replace Model.parse_obj(data) with Model.model_validate(data).
Replace Model.parse_obj(data) with Model(**data).
Replace Model.schema() with Model.model_json_schema().
Replace .copy(update=...) with .model_copy(update=...).
Replace .copy(update=...) with Model(**{**obj.model_dump(), **update}).
Replace Model.__fields__ with Model.model_fields; field.required becomes field.is_required(), outer_type_ becomes annotation.
Set model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True) and replace Model.from_orm(obj) with Model.model_validate(obj).
Replace Model.construct(**data) with Model.model_construct(**data).
Replace .dict(...) with .model_dump(...), keeping the same keyword arguments.
Replace .dict() with dict(obj) and filter keys by hand.
Import Field from pydantic and declare `key: Union[int, str] = Field(union_mode="left_to_right")` so the `int` branch is tried first and numeric strings are parsed as integers.
Add a `@field_validator("key", mode="before")` that converts string values matching an integer representation to `int` before union validation, leaving non-numeric strings unchanged.
Import ConfigDict from pydantic and set `model_config = ConfigDict(coerce_numbers_to_str=True)` on `Label`, allowing numeric `sku` inputs to be converted to strings.
Add a `@field_validator("sku", mode="before")` that returns `str(value)` for integer inputs, so `sku` is a string before normal field validation.
In `from_sensor`, pass `int(reading)` as `units` when constructing `StockLevel`, so fractional sensor readings are truncated before integer validation.
Add a Pydantic v2 `@field_validator("units", mode="before")` that converts float inputs to `int`, truncating fractional values before `StockLevel` validates the field.
Replace the `parse_obj_as` import and call with `TypeAdapter` from Pydantic: return `TypeAdapter(List[User]).validate_python(rows)`.
Remove the `parse_obj_as` import and validate each row with the v2 API: return `[User.model_validate(row) for row in rows]`.

Replace `ProfilePatch(**raw).__fields_set__` with `ProfilePatch(**raw).model_fields_set` to use Pydantic v2’s supported API for retrieving explicitly supplied fields.
Replace the deprecated field-set access with `ProfilePatch(**raw).model_dump(exclude_unset=True).keys()` so only fields explicitly supplied in `raw` are returned.
Add a Pydantic v2 `@field_serializer("price")` to `Quote` that returns `float(value)`. Then `model_dump(mode="json")` emits `price` as a JSON number.

Change `publish` to call `json.dumps(q.model_dump(mode="python"), default=float)`. The JSON encoder fallback converts the `Decimal` price to a JSON number instead of the string produced by JSON-mode dumping.

Import `field_serializer` from Pydantic and add a serializer to `Shift`: `@field_serializer("started")` followed by a method that returns `value.isoformat()`. This preserves the `+00:00` offset instead of emitting `Z`.
Change `to_wire` to dump in Python mode, replace the `started` value in the resulting dict with `s.started.isoformat()`, then pass that dict to `json.dumps`. This explicitly emits `+00:00` for UTC.
